editorial:
Imagine jumping back into the early eighties where everything feels loud and reckless. You get to follow a group of friends just trying to figure out how to be adults without any real guidance. You have Bill, who is just trying to make his new apartment work, and Jim, who is basically a human wrecking ball. Then there is Tom, who is just completely out there, and Anita, who is playing a dangerous game by dating an older guy named David. It feels like a chaotic summer break that never ends, filled with bad decisions and plenty of laughs. The vibe is very loose and messy, which makes it feel like you are hanging out with these people in real life.

The acting feels natural because the characters aren't trying too hard to be heroes. You will love the funny banter and the way the plot just wanders from one crazy situation to the next. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the energy usually picks back up right when you might get bored. If you love nostalgic teen movies, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that these characters are still pretty lost, but they have each other. After all the wild parties and relationship drama, Anita realizes that David is not the savior she thought he was. The group ends up accepting that growing up is messy and doesn't happen overnight. It ends on a hopeful but realistic note, leaving you feeling like they will probably get into more trouble tomorrow.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves retro teen comedies and coming-of-age stories.
